docs.title: crawl_github_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def crawl_github_files(repo_url, token=None, max_file_size: int = 1 * 1024 * 1024, use_relative_paths: bool = False, include_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None, exclude_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None) -> dict:

Description: Crawls files from a specific path in a GitHub repository at a designated commit, branch, or tag. It selects between an ephemeral local SSH clone or recursive GitHub REST API v3 queries based on the format of repo_url. During traversal, it enforces pattern filtering, .gitignore compliance, size thresholds, and text-only encoding validation, returning a unified dictionary containing the file contents map and crawl statistics.

Parameters: * repo_url (str): Target GitHub repository URL. Supports SSH cloning URLs (e.g., git@github.com:... or URLs ending in .git) and standard web URLs specifying branches, commits, or subdirectories (e.g., https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/commit_hash/path/to/dir). * token (str | None, optional): GitHub Personal Access Token. Required for private repositories and recommended for public repositories to raise the default GitHub REST API hourly rate limit. Defaults to None. * max_file_size (int, optional): Maximum allowable file size in bytes to download or read. Defaults to 1 MB (1048576 bytes). * use_relative_paths (bool, optional): When True, emitted file keys are made relative to the specified subdirectory rather than the repository root. Defaults to False. * include_patterns (str | set[str] | None, optional): A glob pattern or set of glob patterns specifying which file names to include (e.g., "*.py"). If None, all encountered files are included by default. * exclude_patterns (str | set[str] | None, optional): A glob pattern or set of glob patterns specifying which file paths or directory names to exclude. Defaults to None.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary containing two keys: "files" (mapping file paths to extracted string contents) and "stats" (metadata covering skipped counts, patterns applied, base paths, and execution sources).

Raises: * ValueError: Raised when an HTTP(S) URL cannot be parsed into at least repository owner and repository name components. * Exception: Raised when GitHub API rate limits are encountered and no token was provided to permit sleep backoff or authenticated elevation.

docs.title: Phase 1: Parameter Normalization and Pattern Sanitization
docs.text:
# Convert single pattern to set
    if include_patterns and isinstance(include_patterns, str):
        include_patterns = {include_patterns}
    if exclude_patterns and isinstance(exclude_patterns, str):
        exclude_patterns = {exclude_patterns}
The entry sequence validates and normalizes the pattern matching parameters. Incoming string literals for both inclusion and exclusion are cast into Python sets to guarantee consistent O(1) membership checks and uniform iteration across downstream filtering steps. This prevents subtle type-checking errors when callers provide single pattern strings (e.g., "*.py") instead of collections.

docs.title: Phase 2: SSH Repository Clone and Local Inspection
docs.text:
# Detect SSH URL (git@ or .git suffix)
    is_ssh_url = repo_url.startswith("git@") or repo_url.endswith(".git")

    if is_ssh_url:
        # Clone repo via SSH to temp dir
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdirname:
            emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"Cloning SSH repo {repo_url} to temp dir {tmpdirname} ...")
            try:
                repo = git.Repo.clone_from(repo_url, tmpdirname)
            except Exception as e:
                emit_raw("ERROR", f"Error cloning repo: {e}")
                return {"files": {}, "stats": {"error": str(e)}}
If the repository string matches SSH protocol conventions (prefixed with git@ or ending with .git), the crawler uses tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() to create an isolated scratchpad workspace. It uses GitPython's git.Repo.clone_from() method to clone the remote repository into this temporary directory. If network failure, missing SSH keys, or authentication errors occur, the method traps the generic exception, emits an error log using emit_raw(), and returns an empty files dictionary with an error payload in the statistics block.

docs.title: Phase 3: Local Gitignore Ingestion and Directory Pruning
docs.text:
# --- Load .gitignore ---
            gitignore_path = os.path.join(tmpdirname, ".gitignore")
            gitignore_spec = None
            if os.path.exists(gitignore_path):
                try:
                    with open(gitignore_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                        gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", f.readlines())
                    emit("CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED", path="repository")
                except Exception:
                    pass

            for root, dirs, filenames in os.walk(tmpdirname):
                # Filter directories
                excluded_dirs = set()
                for d in sorted(dirs):
                    dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), tmpdirname)
                    reason = None
                    if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
                        reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_GITIGNORE")
                    elif exclude_patterns:
                        for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                            dir_pattern = pattern.removesuffix("/*")
                            if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                                reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_EXCLUDED")
                                break

                    if reason:
                        excluded_dirs.add(d)
                        entry_num += 1
                        count_excluded += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_DIR_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=dirpath_rel, reason=reason)

                for d in dirs.copy():
                    if d in excluded_dirs:
                        dirs.remove(d)

                # Sort remaining dirs for consistent traversal order
                dirs.sort()
The crawler reads .gitignore from the root of the cloned repository and compiles it using pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", ...). During os.walk(), the subdirectories under dirs are evaluated against both the gitignore specification and user-provided exclude_patterns. Any matched directory is added to excluded_dirs and purged in-place from dirs via dirs.remove(d). This optimization prevents os.walk from descending into ignored directory trees (such as .git, node_modules, or vendor directories), saving I/O operations and memory.

docs.title: Phase 4: Local File Ingestion and Size Guardrails
docs.text:
for filename in sorted(filenames):
                    abs_path = os.path.join(root, filename)
                    rel_path = os.path.relpath(abs_path, tmpdirname)
                    entry_num += 1

                    # Check include/exclude patterns
                    if not should_include_file(rel_path, filename, gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
                        count_excluded += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                        continue

                    # Check file size
                    try:
                        file_size = os.path.getsize(abs_path)
                    except OSError:
                        continue

                    if file_size > max_file_size:
                        count_size_limit += 1
                        skipped_size_list.append(rel_path)
                        size_kb = file_size / 1024
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                        continue

                    # Read content
                    try:
                        with open(abs_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                            content = f.read()
                        files[rel_path] = content
                        count_processed += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                        count_non_text += 1
                        skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    except Exception as e:
                        count_non_text += 1
                        skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_ERROR", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, error=e)
For every file in allowed directories, the crawler constructs relative and absolute paths and passes them through should_include_file(). If included, it reads the file size using os.getsize(). Files larger than max_file_size are skipped, tracked in skipped_size_list, and reported via emit(). Valid files are read using utf-8-sig encoding (handling optional UTF-8 Byte Order Marks). Any decoding errors (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError) identify the file as binary or unsupported non-text, redirecting it to the skipped_non_text_list without aborting the walk.

docs.title: Phase 5: GitHub URL Parsing and Tree Target Resolution
docs.text:
# Parse GitHub URL to extract owner, repo, commit/branch, and path
    parsed_url = urlparse(repo_url)
    path_parts = parsed_url.path.strip("/").split("/")

    if len(path_parts) < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid GitHub URL: {repo_url}")

    # Extract the basic components
    owner = path_parts[0]
    repo = path_parts[1]

    # Setup for GitHub API
    headers = {"Accept": "application/vnd.github.v3+json"}
    if token:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"token {token}"
// ...
    # Check if URL contains a specific branch/commit
    if len(path_parts) > 3 and path_parts[2] == "tree":

        def join_parts(i):
            return "/".join(path_parts[i:])

        branches = fetch_branches(owner, repo)
        branch_names = (branch.get("name") for branch in branches)

        # Fetching branches was not successful
        if len(branches) == 0:
            return None

        # Check branch name
        relevant_path = join_parts(3)

        # Find a match with relevant path and get the branch name
        filter_gen = (name for name in branch_names if relevant_path.startswith(name))
        ref = next(filter_gen, None)

        # If match is not found, check for is it a tree
        if ref is None:
            tree = path_parts[3]
            ref = tree if check_tree(owner, repo, tree) else None

        # If it is neither a tree nor a branch name
        if ref is None:
            emit_raw("ERROR", "The given path does not match with any branch and any tree in the repository.\nPlease verify the path is exists.")
            return None

        # Combine all parts after the ref as the path
        part_index = 5 if "/" in ref else 4
        specific_path = join_parts(part_index) if part_index < len(path_parts) else ""
    else:
        # Don't put the ref param in query
        # and let Github decide default branch
        ref = None
        specific_path = ""
For non-SSH targets, the crawler parses the URL path using urllib.parse.urlparse. If the URL contains the /tree/ token, it splits the URL path into owner, repository name, target reference, and optional subdirectory path. Because branch names can contain forward slashes (e.g., feature/login), the crawler queries the repository's active branch names using fetch_branches() and checks if the path starts with any known branch name. If branch matching fails, it verifies whether the token represents a direct commit SHA using check_tree(). Once the ref is resolved, all subsequent path elements are concatenated into specific_path.

docs.title: Phase 6: Remote Gitignore Ingestion via API
docs.text:
# --- Try to fetch .gitignore ---
    gitignore_spec = None
    try:
        gi_url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/.gitignore"
        gi_params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}
        gi_resp = requests.get(gi_url, headers=headers, params=gi_params, timeout=(10, 10))
        if gi_resp.status_code == 200:
            gi_data = gi_resp.json()
            if "content" in gi_data and gi_data.get("encoding") == "base64":
                gi_content = base64.b64decode(gi_data["content"]).decode("utf-8")
                gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", gi_content.splitlines())
                emit("CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED", path="repository (API)")
    except Exception:
        pass
Before recursively crawling directory nodes via the GitHub API, the function attempts to retrieve .gitignore from the root of the specified reference. It makes an HTTP GET request to /contents/.gitignore with a (10, 10) second timeout. If the file is present, the base64 content payload is decoded into a string, converted into lines, and compiled into a pathspec.PathSpec matcher. If the file does not exist (HTTP 404) or encounters network faults, the exception is caught, and gitignore_spec remains None without halting the crawl.

docs.title: should_include_file()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Closure inside crawl_github_files) Signature: def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether a given file path should be included in the crawl based on include patterns, .gitignore rules, and exclude patterns.

    def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:
        """Determine if a file should be included based on patterns"""
        # If no include patterns are specified, include all files
        if not include_patterns:
            include_file = True
        else:
            # Check if file matches any include pattern
            include_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_name, pattern) for pattern in include_patterns)

        # Check gitignore if provided
        if include_file and gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path):
            return False

        # If exclude patterns are specified, check if file should be excluded
        if exclude_patterns and include_file:
            # Exclude if file matches any exclude pattern
            exclude_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, pattern) for pattern in exclude_patterns)
            return not exclude_file

        return include_file
The helper evaluates files using a multi-step filter chain. First, it matches file_name against include_patterns via fnmatch.fnmatch; if include_patterns is empty or None, the file passes by default. Next, if an active gitignore_spec is provided and matches the relative file_path, the file is rejected immediately. Finally, if exclude_patterns are defined, the method checks the relative file_path against each pattern; a match results in rejection. The file is accepted only if it satisfies all three filter stages.

Parameters: * file_path (str): Relative path of the candidate file from the crawl root. * file_name (str): The basename of the file (used for include pattern evaluation). * gitignore_spec (pathspec.PathSpec | None, optional): Compiled gitignore spec instance. Defaults to None.

Returns: * bool: True if the file passes all inclusion and exclusion checks; False otherwise.

Example: 

# Called internally during directory walks and API contents processing:
if not should_include_file(rel_path, filename, gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
    count_excluded += 1
    emit("CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
    continue

docs.title: fetch_branches()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Closure inside crawl_github_files) Signature: def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str) -> list[dict]:

Description: Queries the GitHub REST API for all branches in the target repository to help resolve branch names embedded within URL paths.

    def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str):
        """Get branches of the repository"""

        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches"
        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")

        if response.status_code == 404:
            if not token:
                emit_raw(
                    "ERROR",
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or is private.\n"
                    "If this is a private repository, please provide a valid GitHub token via the 'token' argument or set the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable.",
                )
            else:
                emit_raw(
                    "ERROR",
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or insufficient permissions with the provided token.\n"
                    "Please verify the repository exists and the token has access to this repository.",
                )
            return []

        if response.status_code != 200:
            emit_raw("ERROR", f"Error fetching the branches of {owner}/{repo}: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")
            return []

        return response.json()
The helper issues a synchronous GET request to /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches with a 30-second timeout. If unauthenticated requests receive an HTTP 403 or 429 response, it raises an exception indicating that the rate limit was exceeded. For HTTP 404 responses, it distinguishes between unauthenticated requests (which may indicate a private repository) and authenticated requests with invalid tokens, logging the appropriate diagnostic via emit_raw(). When the response code is 200, it parses and returns the branch metadata payload as a list of dictionaries.

Parameters: * owner (str): Repository owner username or organization. * repo (str): Target repository name.

Returns: * list[dict]: Parsed JSON list of branch descriptor objects (containing branch name, commit, etc.), or an empty list upon failure.

Raises: * Exception: If rate limits (HTTP 403 or 429) are encountered when crawling without an authentication token.

Example: 

# Called internally when parsing URLs containing a tree reference:
branches = fetch_branches(owner, repo)
branch_names = (branch.get("name") for branch in branches)

docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Closure inside crawl_github_files) Signature: def check_tree(owner: str, repo: str, tree: str) -> bool:

Description: Verifies whether a given commit SHA or tree reference exists in the remote GitHub repository.

    def check_tree(owner: str, repo: str, tree: str):
        """Check the repository has the given tree"""

        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{tree}"
        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")

        return response.status_code == 200
This function targets the /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{tree} endpoint to verify whether an ambiguous path element in a /tree/... URL corresponds to a valid Git tree object or commit SHA rather than a branch name. It enforces rate-limit detection for unauthenticated requests and returns a boolean indicating whether the tree reference was found.

Parameters: * owner (str): Repository owner username or organization. * repo (str): Target repository name. * tree (str): Git commit SHA, branch identifier, or tree hash to validate.

Returns: * bool: True if the API returns an HTTP 200 status code confirming the tree exists; False otherwise.

Raises: * Exception: If rate limits (HTTP 403 or 429) are encountered without an authentication token.

Example:

if ref is None:
    tree = path_parts[3]
    ref = tree if check_tree(owner, repo, tree) else None

docs.title: fetch_contents()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Closure inside crawl_github_files) Signature: def fetch_contents(path: str) -> None:

Description: Recursively queries the GitHub /contents/{path} API endpoint to traverse directories, download raw text file payloads, decode base64 representations, and populate the parent files dictionary.

docs.title: Phase 1: API Request and Rate-Limit Backoff Loop
docs.text:
def fetch_contents(path):
        """Fetch contents of the repository at a specific path and commit"""
        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}"
        params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}

        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and "rate limit exceeded" in response.text.lower():
            if not token:
                raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")
            reset_time = int(response.headers.get("X-RateLimit-Reset", 0))
            wait_time = max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1
            emit_raw("WARNING", f"Rate limit exceeded. Waiting for {wait_time:.0f} seconds...")
            time.sleep(wait_time)
            return fetch_contents(path)

        if response.status_code == 404:
            if not token:
                emit_raw(
                    "ERROR",
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or is private.\n"
                    "If this is a private repository, please provide a valid GitHub token via the 'token' argument or set the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable.",
                )
            elif not path and ref == "main":
                emit_raw(
                    "ERROR",
                    "Error 404: Repository not found. Check if the default branch is not 'main'\n"
                    "Try adding branch name to the request i.e. python main.py --repo https://github.com/username/repo/tree/master",
                )
            else:
                emit_raw(
                    "ERROR",
                    f"Error 404: Path '{path}' not found in repository or insufficient permissions with the provided token.\n"
                    f"Please verify the token has access to this repository and the path exists.",
                )
            return None

        if response.status_code != 200:
            emit_raw("ERROR", f"Error fetching {path}: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")
            return None

        contents = response.json()
The helper constructs the /contents/{path} endpoint, appending the ref query parameter if resolved. When rate limits occur, it parses the X-RateLimit-Reset response header to calculate the required sleep duration, pauses execution via time.sleep(), and retries the request. If the path does not exist, it analyzes the request context (token presence, default branch name) to emit helpful diagnostic messages before aborting the current traversal branch.

docs.title: Phase 2: Directory Child Iteration and Relative Path Resolution
docs.text:
# Handle both single file and directory responses
        if not isinstance(contents, list):
            contents = [contents]

        for item in contents:
            item_path = item["path"]

            # Calculate relative path if requested
            if use_relative_paths and specific_path:
                # Make sure the path is relative to the specified subdirectory
                if item_path.startswith(specific_path):
                    rel_path = item_path[len(specific_path) :].lstrip("/")
                else:
                    rel_path = item_path
            else:
                rel_path = item_path
GitHub's /contents/ endpoint returns a single dictionary when pointing directly to a file and a list of dictionaries when targeting a directory. The helper normalizes single dictionaries into a one-element list. It then computes rel_path for each child item by trimming specific_path prefixes when use_relative_paths is enabled.

docs.title: Phase 3: Raw File Download with Base64 Fallback
docs.text:
if item["type"] == "file":
                api_counters["entry"] += 1
                entry_num = api_counters["entry"]

                # Check if file should be included based on patterns
                if not should_include_file(rel_path, item["name"], gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
                    api_counters["excluded"] += 1
                    emit("CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    continue

                # Check file size if available
                file_size = item.get("size", 0)
                if file_size > max_file_size:
                    api_counters["size_limit"] += 1
                    api_skipped_size.append(rel_path)
                    size_kb = file_size / 1024
                    emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                    continue

                # For files, get raw content
                if item.get("download_url"):
                    file_url = item["download_url"]
                    file_response = requests.get(file_url, headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))

                    # Final size check in case content-length header is available but differs from metadata
                    content_length = int(file_response.headers.get("content-length", 0))
                    if content_length > max_file_size:
                        api_counters["size_limit"] += 1
                        api_skipped_size.append(rel_path)
                        size_kb = content_length / 1024
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                        continue

                    if file_response.status_code == 200:
                        files[rel_path] = file_response.text
                        api_counters["processed"] += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    else:
                        api_counters["non_text"] += 1
                        api_skipped_non_text.append(rel_path)
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_HTTP_ERROR", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, status=file_response.status_code)
                else:
                    # Alternative method if download_url is not available
                    content_response = requests.get(item["url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
                    if content_response.status_code == 200:
                        content_data = content_response.json()
                        if content_data.get("encoding") == "base64" and "content" in content_data:
                            # Check size of base64 content before decoding
                            if len(content_data["content"]) * 0.75 > max_file_size:  # Approximate size calculation
                                estimated_size = int(len(content_data["content"]) * 0.75)
                                api_counters["size_limit"] += 1
                                api_skipped_size.append(rel_path)
                                size_kb = estimated_size / 1024
                                emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                                continue

                            file_content = base64.b64decode(content_data["content"]).decode("utf-8")
                            files[rel_path] = file_content
                            api_counters["processed"] += 1
                            emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
// ...
For items marked as file, the helper verifies inclusion criteria and checks the file's reported size against max_file_size. If valid, it downloads the raw text using item["download_url"]. If download_url is missing, it falls back to requesting item["url"], which returns JSON containing base64-encoded file data. It estimates the payload size (len * 0.75) to avoid decoding oversized files, decodes the base64 content into UTF-8 text, and stores the resulting string in the files dictionary.

docs.title: Phase 4: Recursive Directory Traversal
docs.text:
elif item["type"] == "dir":
                # Check if directory should be excluded before recursing
                dir_excluded = False
                dir_reason = None

                if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(rel_path):
                    dir_excluded = True
                    dir_reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_GITIGNORE")

                if not dir_excluded and exclude_patterns:
                    dir_name = item["name"]  # basename of the directory
                    for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                        dir_pattern = pattern.removesuffix("/*")

                            fnmatch.fnmatch(item_path, dir_pattern)

                            dir_reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_EXCLUDED")
                            break

                if dir_excluded:
                    api_counters["entry"] += 1
                    api_counters["excluded"] += 1
                    emit("CRAWL_DIR_EXCLUDED", num=api_counters["entry"], path=rel_path, reason=dir_reason)

If excluded, it increments the exclusion counters, emits an exclusion log, and skips the directory. Otherwise, it makes a recursive call to fetch_contents(item_path) to crawl the subdirectory.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: The module handles remote network failures, API constraints, and file system anomalies across both ingestion paths:

docs.title: GitHub REST API Rate Limiting (HTTP 403 / 429)
docs.text:
• Unauthenticated Requests: If the API responds with HTTP 403 or 429 and no token was provided, the function raises an Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var."). This halts execution immediately to alert the operator.
  • Authenticated Requests with Backoff: When a token is present and the response contains "rate limit exceeded", the function reads the X-RateLimit-Reset HTTP header, calculates the wait time (max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1), logs a warning via emit_raw(), sleeps using time.sleep(wait_time), and transparently retries fetch_contents().

docs.title: Missing Repositories and Reference Failures (HTTP 404)
docs.text:
• Private vs Missing Repositories: On HTTP 404 responses, the engine checks whether a token was provided. If missing, it notes that the repository may be private and require authentication. If a token was provided, it reports that permissions are insufficient or the target path does not exist.
  • Default Branch Mismatches: If traversing the repository root on ref main returns a 404, the engine logs a suggestion to verify if the default branch is named master.

docs.title: Encoding Failures and Binary Detection
docs.text:
• Cloned Repositories: During local filesystem reads, file opens specify encoding="utf-8-sig". If reading raises UnicodeDecodeError or ValueError, the engine catches the exception, classifies the file as non-text, increments count_non_text, and continues traversing without failing.
  • API Ingestion: Files downloaded without a download_url fallback to base64 decoding via base64.b64decode(). If the decoded bytes cannot be parsed as UTF-8, or if the JSON payload lacks expected content structures, the file is logged as non-text and safely skipped.

docs.title: Git Clone Faults
docs.text: • During the SSH clone workflow, calls to git.Repo.clone_from() are wrapped in a generic try...except Exception block. If cloning fails (due to invalid host keys, unauthenticated SSH tokens, or network drops), the error is intercepted, logged via emit_raw("ERROR", ...), and returned safely in the stats dictionary: {"files": {}, "stats": {"error": str(e)}}.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The crawl_local_files.py module serves as the primary filesystem ingestion engine within the knowledge extraction pipeline. While its sibling component, crawl_github_files.py, provides ingestion over remote GitHub repositories via API queries or ephemeral Git clones, crawl_local_files.py executes synchronous, local directory traversals. It presents a structurally symmetric interface to downstream pipeline consumers, accepting path inclusion and exclusion rules and returning an in-memory dictionary mapping discovered file paths directly to their decoded text content.

Operating directly on the host filesystem via Python's standard os.walk iterator, the module enforces a multi-phase pruning and filtering workflow. As it encounters directories, it dynamically locates, parses, and stacks local .gitignore files using pathspec, ensuring that scoped exclusion rules defined at any directory tier take immediate effect. Directories matching exclusion patterns or .gitignore specifications are pruned in-place from the traversal stack, avoiding costly filesystem traversal into large trees like node_modules, .git, or build outputs. Files that pass structural checks are evaluated for size thresholds, opened using utf-8-sig encoding to handle optional Byte Order Marks, and gracefully skipped if binary or corrupt.

Throughout execution, the module integrates tightly with the runtime output bus via utils/output.py. Instead of writing directly to standard streams or raising non-critical filesystem exceptions, the crawler emits fine-grained lifecycle and diagnostic events (CRAWL_DIR_EXCLUDED, CRAWL_FILE_GITIGNORE, CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT, CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED). This ensures high-visibility operational metrics and seamless localization support across the document synthesis lifecycle.

docs.title: crawl_local_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def crawl_local_files(directory, include_patterns=None, exclude_patterns=None, max_file_size=None, use_relative_paths=True)

Description: Crawls a target local directory tree, applying hierarchical .gitignore rules, inclusion globs, exclusion globs, and maximum file size boundaries. Discovered readable text files are decoded and assembled into a path-to-content map. Operational metrics and skipping events are emitted directly to the logging system.

Parameters: * directory (str): Target filesystem directory path to crawl. * include_patterns (set[str], optional): Set of Unix glob patterns that files must match to be included (e.g., {"*.py", "*.js"}). Defaults to None. * exclude_patterns (set[str], optional): Set of Unix glob patterns specifying files or directories to exclude (e.g., {"tests/*", "*.pyc"}). Defaults to None. * max_file_size (int, optional): Maximum permissible file size in bytes. Files exceeding this threshold are bypassed. Defaults to None. * use_relative_paths (bool): If True, keys in the returned dictionary are paths relative to directory; if False, keys are absolute or raw joined filesystem paths. Defaults to True.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary containing a single key "files", mapped to a sub-dictionary of {filepath: content}.

Raises: * ValueError: If directory does not exist or does not point to a valid directory on the host filesystem.

The function executes across six discrete operational phases detailed below.

docs.title: Phase 1: Directory Validation and Baseline Setup
docs.text:
if not os.path.isdir(directory):
        raise ValueError(f"Directory does not exist: {directory}")

    files_dict = {}

    # --- Counters ---
    entry_num = 0
    count_processed = 0
    count_excluded = 0
    count_size_limit = 0
    count_non_text = 0
    skipped_size_limit = []
    skipped_non_text = []

    # --- Gitignore specs: {abs_dir_path: pathspec} ---
    gitignore_specs = {}
    root_gi_path = os.path.join(directory, ".gitignore")
    if os.path.exists(root_gi_path):
        spec = _load_gitignore(root_gi_path)
        if spec:
            gitignore_specs[os.path.abspath(directory)] = spec
            emit("CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED", path=root_gi_path)

    # Translated reason strings (looked up once)
    reason_excluded = get("CRAWL_REASON_EXCLUDED")
    reason_gitignore = get("CRAWL_REASON_GITIGNORE")
This phase enforces initial precondition checks by asserting that the target path resolves to an active directory via os.path.isdir. It instantiates the result payload map files_dict alongside metric counters for entries processed, excluded, bounded by file size, or flagged as non-text. The crawler initializes gitignore_specs as an empty dictionary and attempts to load an initial .gitignore at the root directory level via _load_gitignore(). If a valid root .gitignore is found, its compiled pathspec.PathSpec is bound to the directory's absolute path, and an informational event (CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED) is broadcast. Localized exclusion reason tokens are queried from the output catalog once to optimize loop performance.

docs.title: Phase 2: Dynamic GitIgnore Specification Registry
docs.text:
# --- Single-pass: walk, filter, and process inline ---
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(directory):
        abs_root = os.path.abspath(root)

        # Check for nested .gitignore in current directory (skip root, already loaded)
        if abs_root != os.path.abspath(directory):
            nested_gi = os.path.join(root, ".gitignore")
            if os.path.exists(nested_gi):
                spec = _load_gitignore(nested_gi)
                if spec:
                    gitignore_specs[abs_root] = spec
The traversal initiates a single-pass iteration using os.walk(directory). At each directory tier, the crawler converts root to an absolute path (abs_root) and inspects whether a nested .gitignore file exists within that subdirectory. To prevent redundant I/O, the root directory is bypassed since it was parsed in Phase 1. When a nested .gitignore is found, _load_gitignore() compiles its rules into a new PathSpec and registers it in gitignore_specs keyed by abs_root. This enables downward-cascading rule scoping that mirrors standard Git behavior.

docs.title: Phase 3: Directory Traversal and In-Place Pruning
docs.text:
# --- Directory filtering ---
        excluded_dirs = set()
        for d in sorted(dirs):
            abs_d = os.path.join(abs_root, d)
            dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(abs_d, directory)

            reason = None
            if _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_d, is_dir=True):
                reason = reason_gitignore
            elif exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    dir_pattern = pattern.removesuffix("/*")
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                        reason = reason_excluded
                        break

            if reason:
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                entry_num += 1
                count_excluded += 1
                emit("CRAWL_DIR_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=dirpath_rel, reason=reason)

        for d in dirs.copy():
            if d in excluded_dirs:
                dirs.remove(d)

        # Sort remaining dirs for consistent traversal order
        dirs.sort()
Directory pruning prevents unnecessary filesystem I/O into unneeded directory subtrees. Each subdirectory in dirs is sorted and checked against active gitignore_specs with is_dir=True and tested against caller-specified exclude_patterns. The crawler cleans wildcards using removesuffix("/*") to test against both relative directory paths and individual segment names using fnmatch.fnmatch. If excluded, an exclusion event is emitted, and the directory name is staged in excluded_dirs. Crucially, matching directories are removed directly from dirs in-place using dirs.remove(d). This mutates the iterator list utilized by os.walk, preventing it from descending into excluded branches entirely. The remaining entries in dirs are sorted to guarantee deterministic alphabetical traversal order.

docs.title: Phase 4: Per-File Pattern Filtering
docs.text:
# --- File processing (inline, sorted) ---
        for filename in sorted(files):
            filepath = os.path.join(root, filename)
            abs_filepath = os.path.abspath(filepath)
            relpath = os.path.relpath(filepath, directory) if use_relative_paths else filepath
            entry_num += 1

            # Check gitignore (all levels)
            if _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_filepath):
                count_excluded += 1
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_GITIGNORE", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
                continue

            # Check exclude patterns
            excluded = False
            if exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(relpath, pattern):
                        excluded = True
                        break
            if excluded:
                count_excluded += 1
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
                continue

            # Check include patterns
            if include_patterns:
                matched = False
                for pattern in include_patterns:
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(relpath, pattern):
                        matched = True
                        break
                if not matched:
                    count_excluded += 1
                    emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_INCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
                    continue
In this phase, individual files within the current directory are sorted and evaluated sequentially against exclusion boundaries. A candidate file's absolute path is checked against all active gitignore_specs via _matches_any_gitignore(); if matched, count_excluded increments, a CRAWL_FILE_GITIGNORE event is emitted, and execution continues to the next candidate. Next, if exclude_patterns are provided, the file's normalized relative path is evaluated via fnmatch. Finally, if explicit include_patterns are provided, the path must match at least one inclusion rule; failure to match triggers a CRAWL_FILE_NOT_INCLUDED event and bypasses further reading.

docs.title: Phase 5: File Ingestion and Unicode Decoding
docs.text:
# Check size limit
            if max_file_size and os.path.getsize(filepath) > max_file_size:
                count_size_limit += 1
                skipped_size_limit.append(relpath)
                size_kb = os.path.getsize(filepath) / 1024
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=relpath, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                continue

            # Try to read as text
            try:
                with open(filepath, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                files_dict[relpath] = content
                count_processed += 1
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
            except Exception as e:
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_ERROR", num=entry_num, path=relpath, error=e)
Files passing pattern filtering are evaluated against max_file_size. If the byte size returned by os.path.getsize exceeds the threshold, the relative path is added to skipped_size_limit and skipped. For permitted files, the crawler reads the content using the utf-8-sig codec, which decodes UTF-8 while stripping BOM headers. If decoding raises UnicodeDecodeError or ValueError, the file is marked as non-text, added to skipped_non_text, and skipped. Any unexpected I/O or permission errors are trapped by the general Exception clause, which logs CRAWL_FILE_ERROR without terminating the crawl. Successfully ingested text files are stored in files_dict under relpath.

docs.title: Phase 6: Telemetry Reporting and Payload Assembly
docs.text:
# --- Summary ---
    total_fetched = count_processed + count_excluded + count_size_limit + count_non_text
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_HEADER")
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_TOTAL", count=total_fetched)
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_PROCESSED", count=count_processed)
    if count_excluded > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED", count=count_excluded)
    if count_size_limit > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_SIZE_LIMIT", count=count_size_limit)
        for f in skipped_size_limit:
            emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_ITEM", name=f)
    if count_non_text > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_NON_TEXT", count=count_non_text)
        for f in skipped_non_text:
            emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_ITEM", name=f)

    return {"files": files_dict}
Following directory traversal completion, the module compiles summary metrics over all visited entries (total_fetched = count_processed + count_excluded + count_size_limit + count_non_text). It emits structured summary headers and totals, followed by itemized listings of files skipped due to size restrictions or non-text formatting. Finally, it packages the ingested file paths and their contents into the standard dictionary schema {"files": files_dict} and returns it to the caller.

Example: 

# Extracted directly from utils/crawl_local_files.py (__main__ execution block)
files_data = crawl_local_files(
    "..",
    exclude_patterns={
        "*.pyc",
        "__pycache__/*",
        ".venv/*",
        ".git/*",
        "docs/*",
        "output/*",
    },
)
print(f"Found {len(files_data['files'])} files:")
for path in files_data["files"]:
    print(f"  {path}")

docs.title: _load_gitignore()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _load_gitignore(gitignore_path: str) -> Optional[pathspec.PathSpec]:

Description: Opens a specified .gitignore file from the host filesystem, reads its pattern lines, and compiles them into a pathspec.PathSpec object using the standard Git "gitwildmatch" syntax rules. If the file cannot be opened, read, or parsed, the exception is caught and None is returned.

Parameters: * gitignore_path (str): The filesystem path pointing to the .gitignore file.

Returns: * Optional[pathspec.PathSpec]: A compiled path matching specification object if parsed successfully, or None on any I/O or syntax failure.

Raises: * None. All exceptions raised during file reading or parsing are caught internally.

Core Implementation: 

def _load_gitignore(gitignore_path):
    """Load a .gitignore file and return a PathSpec, or None on failure."""
    try:
        with open(gitignore_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
            return pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", f.readlines())
    except Exception:
        return None
The helper wraps file operations in a defensive try...except block to prevent unreadable, locked, or corrupt .gitignore files from aborting the crawl. It opens the target path with utf-8-sig to strip any Byte Order Marks that may precede pattern definitions on Windows platforms. The collected lines are parsed by pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines using Git's wildmatch syntax. Any unexpected errors cause the function to return None, signaling to the caller that no rules could be loaded.

Example: 

# Extracted from crawl_local_files() in utils/crawl_local_files.py
root_gi_path = os.path.join(directory, ".gitignore")
if os.path.exists(root_gi_path):
    spec = _load_gitignore(root_gi_path)
    if spec:
        gitignore_specs[os.path.abspath(directory)] = spec
        emit("CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED", path=root_gi_path)

docs.title: _matches_any_gitignore()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs: dict[str, pathspec.PathSpec], abs_path: str, is_dir: bool = False) -> bool:

Description: Determines if an absolute target path matches any compiled .gitignore specification in gitignore_specs. Because .gitignore rules apply only to files within their own directory subtree, this function calculates the relative path from each .gitignore root to the target path. It normalizes path separators to POSIX slashes and appends a trailing slash for directory checks.

Parameters: * gitignore_specs (dict[str, pathspec.PathSpec]): Mapping of absolute directory paths to their compiled pathspec.PathSpec instances. * abs_path (str): Absolute filesystem path of the candidate file or directory to check. * is_dir (bool): Flag indicating whether abs_path represents a directory. Defaults to False.

Returns: * bool: True if abs_path matches any active .gitignore specification within its scope; otherwise False.

Raises: * None.

Core Implementation: 

def _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_path, is_dir=False):
    for gi_dir, spec in gitignore_specs.items():
        rel = os.path.relpath(abs_path, gi_dir)
        # Skip if the path is not under this gitignore's scope
        if rel.startswith(".."):
            continue
        match_path = rel.replace("\\", "/")
        if is_dir:
            match_path = match_path.rstrip("/") + "/"
        if spec.match_file(match_path):
            return True
    return False
This helper enforces directory-scoped .gitignore semantics. For every registered spec, it computes the relative path rel = os.path.relpath(abs_path, gi_dir). If rel starts with ".." (or Windows "..\\"), the candidate path resides outside that .gitignore file's subtree, and that spec is skipped. For paths within scope, Windows backslashes are replaced with POSIX forward slashes (/) to ensure cross-platform compatibility with pathspec. If is_dir is True, any trailing slash is stripped and re-appended (match_path.rstrip("/") + "/") so directory-only rules (e.g., build/) match correctly. If any specification matches, True is returned immediately.

Example: 

# Extracted from crawl_local_files() in utils/crawl_local_files.py
if _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_d, is_dir=True):
    reason = reason_gitignore
# ...
if _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_filepath):
    count_excluded += 1
    emit("CRAWL_FILE_GITIGNORE", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
    continue

Field Type Description entry_num int Monotonically increasing counter indexing every directory and file encountered. count_processed int Total number of files successfully read, decoded, and stored in files_dict. count_excluded int Total count of directories and files skipped via .gitignore, exclude_patterns, or missing include_patterns. count_size_limit int Total count of files whose size exceeded max_file_size. count_non_text int Total count of files skipped due to binary encoding, decoding errors, or filesystem read faults. skipped_size_limit list[str] List of relative file paths that exceeded max_file_size. skipped_non_text list[str] List of relative file paths flagged as binary or unreadable.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module employs defensive error-handling patterns to ensure that filesystem anomalies, binary payloads, and pattern syntax issues do not terminate ingestion prematurely:

  1. Precondition Directory Validation: crawl_local_files() tests the input path via os.path.isdir(directory) before beginning traversal. If the path does not exist or points to a non-directory file, it raises a ValueError: 

    if not os.path.isdir(directory):
    raise ValueError(f"Directory does not exist: {directory}")

  2. Fault-Tolerant .gitignore Loading: Inside _load_gitignore(), all filesystem access and parsing errors are intercepted via except Exception: return None. If a .gitignore cannot be read due to file permissions or invalid syntax, the crawler ignores that specific file and proceeds without aborting.

  3. Binary and Non-Text Ingestion Handling: Text decoding errors are caught explicitly when reading candidate files: 

    try:
    with open(filepath, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        content = f.read()
    files_dict[relpath] = content
    count_processed += 1
    emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
    count_non_text += 1
    skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
    emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
except Exception as e:
    count_non_text += 1
    skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
    emit("CRAWL_FILE_ERROR", num=entry_num, path=relpath, error=e)

  4. UnicodeDecodeError and ValueError: These indicate non-text or binary files (e.g., compiled .pyc, images, zip archives). The crawler records the path in skipped_non_text, increments count_non_text, and emits CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT.
  5. Generic Exception: Catches unexpected OS-level I/O issues (e.g., filesystem locks, permission denials, broken symlinks). It logs CRAWL_FILE_ERROR with the exception object and allows the traversal to continue.

docs.title: exclude_patterns.py
docs.text: Source: utils/exclude_patterns.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Following the filesystem traversal mechanics detailed in crawl_local_files.py, the utils/exclude_patterns.py module defines the centralized filtering baseline for the codebase crawler infrastructure. Ingesting an entire repository into a Large Language Model (LLM) context window requires strict structural hygiene; raw source repositories consistently contain non-code assets, compiled binaries, vendored packages, lockfiles, temporary caches, and virtual environments. Left unfiltered, these non-textual or machine-generated files cause memory bloat, trigger decoding exceptions, exhaust token budgets, and dilute prompt attention with noise. utils/exclude_patterns.py resolves these issues by supplying an exhaustive, category-indexed set of glob patterns configured to intercept unneeded files and directories before disk read or remote API payload transfer occurs.

The module operates as a declarative configuration layer centered on the DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS constant. The patterns follow POSIX globbing conventions via the Python fnmatch specification, distinguishing directory subtrees from leaf files through trailing /* wildcards. When directory crawling is executed by crawl_local_files.py using os.walk() or by crawl_github_files.py via the GitHub REST and Git tree APIs, traversal engines evaluate candidate paths against this pattern set. Trailing slash patterns empower directory crawlers to prune branches in-place at the root level—mutating directory lists to prevent recursing into massive hierarchies such as node_modules or .git—while extension and exact-match patterns filter individual artifacts.

Beyond optimizing I/O throughput and preventing context saturation, utils/exclude_patterns.py enforces data sanitization and security boundaries. By default, it blocks environment configuration files (.env, .env.*), version control metadata (.git/*, .svn/*), and local developer settings (.vscode/*, .idea/*), preventing the accidental exposure of secrets, API credentials, or machine-specific paths to the inference pipeline. Furthermore, modern development tools and agent rules (.cursor/*, .cursorrules, .windsurf/*, .cline/*) are excluded to avoid prompt injection or recursive context pollution from other AI coding assistants.

docs.title: Public API
docs.text: The module exposes a single public configuration constant, DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS, which represents the canonical exclusion set consumed across the codebase analysis architecture.

docs.title: DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS: set[str]

Description: A comprehensive Python set of glob pattern strings designed for fnmatch wildcard evaluation. Patterns targeting directory subtrees terminate with /* (e.g., node_modules/*, dist/*), instructing the crawler to truncate recursive directory descent. Patterns targeting specific file types utilize standard wildcard extensions (e.g., *.png, *.pyc), and security-critical rules leverage exact matching (e.g., .env, .DS_Store).

The definitions within DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS are categorized into seven structural domains:

docs.title: Phase 1: Media, Data, and Static Assets
docs.text:
DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS = {
    # 1. Media, Data, and Static Assets
    "assets/*",
    "data/*",
    "images/*",
    "public/*",
    "static/*",
    "temp/*",
    "tmp/*",
    "media/*",
    "*.jpg",
    "*.jpeg",
    "*.png",
    "*.gif",
    "*.ico",
    "*.svg",
    "*.webp",
    "*.mp4",
    "*.webm",

This section blocks static binary media, raw datasets, document formats, and archive files. Because LLM inference pipelines operate exclusively on textual semantics, ingesting raster graphics (.png, .jpg), vector files (.svg), video/audio containers (.mp4, .wav), or binary office documents (.pdf, .docx) produces either decoding errors or meaningless token sequences. Additionally, archive formats (.zip, .tar.gz) and designated asset directories (assets/*, static/*, data/*) are excluded to avoid processing large payloads that provide no architectural insight.

Modern frameworks generate complex synthetic files—such as Next.js (.next/*), Nuxt (.nuxt/*), SvelteKit (.svelte-kit/*), and Expo (.expo/*) artifacts—that duplicate underlying source logic in minified or bundled formats. Eliminating directories like dist/*, target/*, and build/*, alongside non-essential contexts like test/*, docs/*, and deprecated/*, ensures that downstream document generators synthesize knowledge only from active, production-grade source code.

Security isolation is simultaneously established by matching .env and .env.* files, preventing sensitive API tokens and credentials from leaking into prompt payloads.

    # ...
This partition provides language-level filtering across Python, Java/JVM, C/C++, and mobile application ecosystems. It skips Python bytecode caches (__pycache__/*, *.pyc), test coverage artifacts (.coverage, htmlcov/*), Java compiled classes and archives (*.class, *.jar, *.war), and compiled native binaries and dynamic libraries (*.o, *.so, *.dylib, *.dll, *.exe). Mobile framework compilation trees such as CocoaPods (ios/Pods/*) and Android Gradle builds (android/app/build/*) are likewise intercepted, preventing binary decoding faults in the crawler.

The final segments eliminate operating system noise, version control internals, developer IDE workspaces, and AI agent configuration files. Standard version control trees (.git/*, .svn/*) contain packed object repositories and commit graphs that must not be ingested as code text. Operating system metadata files (.DS_Store, Thumbs.db) and IDE folders (.vscode/*, .idea/*, .vs/*) reflect personal workstation preferences rather than project architecture. Finally, modern AI workspace configurations (.cursor/*, .windsurf/*, .cline/*, .claude/*) and prompt rules (.cursorrules, .windsurfrules) are omitted to prevent the host LLM from encountering conflicting system instructions or assistant meta-prompts.

Example: 

# Consumption pattern inside utils/crawl_local_files.py
from utils.exclude_patterns import DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS
import fnmatch

# Pruning directory traversal in os.walk
def should_exclude(rel_path: str, exclude_patterns: set[str]) -> bool:
    for pattern in exclude_patterns:
        if fnmatch.fnmatch(rel_path, pattern):
            return True
        if pattern.endswith("/*") and fnmatch.fnmatch(rel_path, pattern[:-2]):
            return True
    return False

# Invocation within os.walk loop
active_excludes = DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS.copy()
# dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if not should_exclude(os.path.join(root, d), active_excludes)]

docs.title: Data Structures
docs.text: The DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS object is an unordered Python set containing 96 unique string patterns. The table below details the data layout, scope of matching, target systems, and technical rationale for each category.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
Because utils/exclude_patterns.py provides only static constant definitions without runtime function invocations, it raises no exceptions directly. However, runtime issues can emerge in consuming modules during pattern evaluation:

  • Path Separator Normalization: Standard fnmatch rules assume POSIX directory separators (/). On Windows platforms, paths returned by os.walk() or os.path.join() utilize backslashes (\). Consuming crawlers must normalize paths (e.g., via path.replace("\\", "/")) prior to evaluating them against DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS. Failure to normalize causes patterns containing / to fail silently, resulting in inadvertent ingestion of directories like node_modules.
  • Directory Wildcard Pruning: Patterns targeting directory subtrees use the /* suffix (such as venv/*). A direct match between a raw directory name (e.g., "venv") and "venv/*" evaluates to False in standard fnmatch.fnmatch() calls. Consuming crawlers must therefore evaluate both the directory name and its trailing slash variant (f"{dirname}/*"), or strip the /* suffix, to ensure directories are pruned before recursing into them.
  • Pattern Extension Safety: When users supply custom exclusion rules via CLI arguments (e.g., --exclude), consuming modules should merge user inputs with DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS into a new set instance. The default set remains immutable at the module level, preventing side effects across isolated crawler runs.

  • token_utils.py — Token quantification utilities that calculate context consumption for files passing the exclusion filter.

docs.title: output.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/output.py

Following the repository hygiene rules established in exclude_patterns.py to prune unwanted files during repository traversal, utils/output.py provides the central presentation and diagnostic logging layer for the entire application. It decouples core pipeline logic from terminal display styling, log serialization, and user-facing internationalization (i18n).

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/output.py acts as the single source of truth for all command-line interface (CLI) rendering, formatted file logging, and localized message resolution across the knowledge base generation pipeline. It unifies terminal feedback with persistent execution logs by intercepting status events, token metrics, and operational warnings. The module routes them through destination dispatch rules (STDOUT, LOG, or BOTH), ANSI color formatting maps, and standard Python logging levels.

The subsystem reads user-facing copy from an external CSV catalog (utils/strings.csv), enabling multi-language support. String entries in the catalog support dynamic parameter injection using standard brace-enclosed tokens. If a configured language contains missing string keys, the module invokes an LLM translation workflow through call_llm.py to translate missing strings in batch mode. It then updates strings.csv on disk with UTF-8 BOM encoding and refreshes the internal memory cache.

Architecturally, the module employs a Singleton-style module-level state pattern. Global variables maintain the active localized dictionary (_strings), active language target, file logger instance, and runtime cache flags. Downstream modules invoke lightweight procedural entry points (emit, emit_raw, get) without maintaining their own formatters, ANSI escape constants, or log handlers.
